## Walkthrough

Adds a shared `ElasticJobAnnotation` constant, implements `IsElasticWorkload()` that checks the feature gate and annotation, updates workload-slicing to use the constant, tightens TAS elastic-workload handling, and updates topology-related tests with the annotation and new sub-cases.

## Changes

**Elastic Job Annotation Consolidation**

|Layer / File(s)|Summary|
|---|---|
|**Annotation constant and elastic workload detection** <br> `pkg/constants/constants.go`, `pkg/workload/workload.go`|Introduced `ElasticJobAnnotation` constant and `IsElasticWorkload()` helper that gates elastic detection on `ElasticJobsViaWorkloadSlices` and validates annotation value.|
|**Workload slicing annotation key consolidation** <br> `pkg/workloadslicing/workloadslicing.go`|Updated `EnabledAnnotationKey` to reference `constants.ElasticJobAnnotation` instead of the hardcoded string.|
|**TAS flavor assigner elastic workload handling** <br> `pkg/scheduler/flavorassigner/tas_flavorassigner.go`|Declared `previousAssignment` unconditionally and restricted elastic-slice processing to workloads where `IsElasticWorkload()` is true and `ElasticJobsViaWorkloadSlicesWithTAS` is enabled.|
|**Test updates for elastic job annotation and topology requests** <br> `pkg/scheduler/flavorassigner/flavorassigner_test.go`|Added `metav1` import, annotated test workloads with the elastic-job annotation in required/preferred/unconstrained topology cases, and added sub-tests asserting topology acceptance for regular jobs under `ElasticJobsViaWorkloadSlicesWithTAS`.|

Thanks for working on this!The fix direction is right. I have left a few comments. I think [this](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kueue/pull/11997/changes#r3376451022) should address your CI failures.

- **pkg/scheduler/flavorassigner/tas_flavorassigner.go:64** by [@sohankunkerkar](https://github.com/sohankunkerkar) — 2026-06-08T21:24:32Z
```diff

-			// Only unconstrained topology is supported with elastic workload slices.
 			var previousAssignment *kueue.TopologyAssignment

+

+			if workload.IsElasticWorkload(wl.Obj) {
```

  This block now runs for elastic workloads even when `ElasticJobsViaWorkloadSlicesWithTAS` is off. On main, the gate check was the outer guard and gate off meant the entire block was skipped. Now the annotation check is the outer guard, so elastic workloads enter the block and immediately hit the "gate not enabled" error. They never get a topology assignment.
  
  Please combine both conditions in the outer guard.
  ```go
  if workload.IsElasticWorkload(wl.Obj) && features.Enabled(features.ElasticJobsViaWorkloadSlicesWithTAS) 
  ```

```diff
 }

```

  Please use `workloadslicing.IsElasticWorkload` instead.
